figure: FIGURE 19.2 — Agent turns: token and KV growth
issue: The figure note asserts a factor that the figure's own parameters do not produce: "tokens per submitted request grow 2.5x under no-prefix reuse (100-request ledger, Table 19-1)". From the figure's own stated inputs (9,200 input + 300 output + 800 + 65 per turn, 4 turns): with prefix reuse the request submits 9,200 + 300 + 4 x 865 = 12,960 tokens; without prefix reuse it submits the full context each turn, 10,365 + 11,230 + 12,095 + 12,960 = 46,650 tokens — a 3.6x ratio, not 2.5x. A benign reading exists (the 100-request ledger may use a different turn-count mix, which would change the ratio), but the note does not say so, so a reader who tries to reproduce 2.5x from the figure fails and cannot tell whether the figure or the ledger is wrong.

Recomputation: 12,960 vs 46,650 -> 3.60x.
acceptance_test: The note states the turn-count mix behind the factor (e.g. "2.5x at the ledger's mean of X turns") and the factor is recomputed from that mix, or the factor is replaced by the figure-derivable 3.6x for the depicted 4-turn request. Table 19-1's turn distribution is cited so the number is checkable.

figure: Figure 19.3 (Turn 4: three state-management policies) — parameter note below the axis
issue: The figure's parameter list is not sufficient to reproduce its own headline number. T (the per-turn tool-output token count) appears twice in the append-only formula but is never given a value, and it is the largest single contributor to the total (2 x 1,700 = 3,400 of 12,965 tokens = 26%). S = 800 is listed but its relationship to I_0 is unstated: if S is not inside I_0, the append-only total becomes 13,765 tokens = 36.1 GB, not 34.0 GB. The single-shot reference (24.9 GB) has no formula at all, so neither of the figure's two headline numbers can be checked from the figure.
evidence: Reconstructed from the printed formula 'append-only total = I_0 + T + O + T + O_final @ 2.62 MB/token' with (I_0 = 9.2K input, S = 800 retrieved, O = 65 generated, O_final = 300 output (once)): 9,200 + 1,700 + 65 + 1,700 + 300 = 12,965 tokens x 2.62144 MB/token = 33,986 MB = 34.0 GB, matching the printed bar. Single-shot = I_0 + O_final = 9,500 tokens x 2.62144 MB = 24,904 MB = 24.9 GB, matching the dashed line. Adding S = 800 to the append-only sum gives 13,765 x 2.62144 = 36.1 GB, which is not any printed value.
acceptance_test: Add 'T = 1,700 tokens per tool turn' and 'S = 800 (already included in I_0)' to the parameter note, and add the single-shot formula 'I_0 + O_final = 9,500 tokens'. Verify that a reader can reproduce both 34.0 GB and 24.9 GB from the figure alone, with no recourse to Fig 19.2.

figure: Figure 20.1 — Fleet capacity vs host count
issue: The legend defines the dotted blue series as S = min(40, C_eff), but the plotted dotted line is a horizontal line at 40 rps across the entire host-count axis. For N below the saturation point, S should coincide with C_eff and rise from the origin; the figure instead visually implies that a zero-host fleet serves 40 rps.
evidence: Legend: 'actually-served demand S = min(40, C_eff) (req/s)'. The dotted line is drawn at y = 40 from x = 0 to x = 60. The caption says the served-demand curve 'flattens at the canonical 40 rps peak once 22 hosts are provisioned', which requires a rising segment before 22 hosts. The dashed C_eff line crosses 40 rps at about 21.3 hosts, so S should be piecewise: S = C_eff for N < ~21.3, then S = 40 for N >= ~21.3.
acceptance_test: Redraw the dotted S curve as the lower envelope of C_eff and the 40 rps cap: it must start at (0,0), follow C_eff until the intersection near 21.3 hosts, then become horizontal at 40 rps. Alternatively, remove S from the legend and label the horizontal line only as the 40 rps demand cap. Re-render and verify that no reader can infer nonzero served demand at N = 0.

figure: Figure 20.1 (Fleet capacity vs host count) — caption, first sentence
issue: The caption's takeaway reads 'the served-demand curve is 21.77 -> 22 req/s at the canonical 40 rps peak'. Three defects in one clause: (a) 21.77 and 22 are host counts, not req/s — the unit is wrong; (b) 21.77 appears nowhere in the figure and is not derivable from the plotted curves, which reach S = 40 req/s at N = 21.30; (c) it contradicts the figure's own annotation 'KV screen only: 21 hosts (ideal / 22 at 95%)'. The sentence also does not describe the served-demand curve, whose value at those N is 40 req/s, not 21.77 or 22.
evidence: From the figure's own legend: C_analytic = N x 17/8.6 = 1.9767 N req/s; C_eff = 0.95 x C_analytic = 1.8779 N; S = min(40, C_eff). S first reaches 40 at N = 40/1.8779 = 21.30 -> 22 whole hosts; at N = 21, C_eff = 39.44 req/s < 40, so 21 hosts does not reach the peak. The figure's vertical dotted lines sit at N = 21 and 22 and the annotation reads 'KV screen only: 21 hosts (ideal / 22 at 95%): served demand plateaus at 40 rps'. Separately, printed page 340 (PDF 360) states the case-(ii) requirement as 21.81 hosts (21.81/0.95 = 23), so the book's two 'unrounded host requirement' numbers (21.77 here, 21.81 there) also disagree and neither is reconciled.
acceptance_test: Rewrite the takeaway as 'the served-demand curve reaches the canonical 40 rps peak at N = 21.30 -> 22 hosts (21 hosts at the ideal rate, 22 with the 5% efficiency derate)'; remove the 'req/s' unit from the host counts; and reconcile 21.77 with the 21.81 used on printed page 340, or state explicitly which screen each number belongs to. Confirm the corrected sentence agrees with the in-figure annotation.

figure: Figure 20.1 — plot area, region labels and shading
issue: The two region labels are unanchored and the shading does not match the label placement. The pink band is the unused-capacity wedge (between C_eff and the 40 rps line), while the blue text 'actually-served demand region' sits below the 40 rps line in an unshaded area. With no leader lines or legend key, a reader can reasonably associate the pink shading with the served-demand region — the opposite of the caption's reading of the two gaps. This is the figure's central visual claim (the difference between unused capacity and served demand), and the encoding currently inverts it.
evidence: Rendered page: the pink shading occupies the band above the horizontal 40 rps dotted line and below the dashed C_eff curve for N > ~21.3; the 'UNUSED capacity (N >= 22): insufficient offered demand; S capped at 40 rps - not scheduling overhead' annotation sits inside that band; the 'actually-served demand region' label is placed at roughly N = 30-45, y = 22-28, i.e. below the 40 rps line and outside the shaded band. Caption: 'above saturation C_eff - S is unused capacity from insufficient offered demand, not scheduling overhead'.
acceptance_test: Either shade the region under S = min(40, C_eff) and leave the unused-capacity wedge unshaded, or add leader lines / a legend key binding each label to its region. Verify at 300 dpi that a reader can name which region is which without reading the caption.

figure: Figure 20.1 — annotation 'KV screen only: 21 hosts (ideal / 22 at 95%)'
issue: The annotation attributes the 21/22 host markers to the 'KV screen', but the only capacity curve in the figure is a throughput / Little's-law construction (17 contexts / 8.6 s per host). No KV-memory-derived capacity line is plotted, so the reader cannot tell whether the KV screen is a separate constraint that happens to coincide with the throughput screen or is the thing that produces the plateau. The caption compounds the ambiguity by naming three distinct screens (KV screen, prefill screen with the p = 0.95 policy derate, and the figure's throughput-efficiency derate) while only one is drawn.

Caption: '(21 ideal / 22 at 95% efficiency on the KV screen) with the p = 0.95 derate on the prefill screen (8) - a policy artifact, not a throughput-efficiency derate'. Printed page 340 (PDF 360) treats the Little's-law view and the KV-residency view as 'the same identity in two views', which is not visible anywhere in this figure.
acceptance_test: Either plot the KV-screen capacity as a second labelled line (or a distinct marker style) so the reader can see whether it binds before or after the throughput screen, or relabel the vertical markers as 'throughput screen: 21 hosts ideal / 22 at 95%' and add one sentence stating the KV screen's role and why it does or does not bind.
